_note: Single source of truth for curated sites. lat/lon in degrees, longitude East-positive. 'snap' = move to the highest LOLA terrain within N metres (rim crests / peaks). Coordinates marked approx are region centres, not exact landing points.

sites.name: Shackleton–de Gerlache Ridge
sites.blurb: The ridge connecting Shackleton and de Gerlache craters — one of the most persistently sunlit spots on the Moon.

sites.name: Shackleton Crater Floor
sites.blurb: A permanently shadowed region ~2.8 km below the rim. Water ice may survive here because the Sun never rises above the crater wall.

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.blurb: A 5 km-high mountain and Artemis III candidate region. Tall enough to see Earth more often than the lowlands around it.

sites.name: IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton)
sites.blurb: Intuitive Machines' 2025 lander on the Mons Mouton plateau — the southernmost landing attempt to date.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus (Malapert A)
sites.blurb: First US soft landing since Apollo (Feb 2024), near Malapert A crater.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram
sites.blurb: India's 2023 lander — the first near the south polar region. It ran for one lunar day, then froze in the lunar night.

sites.name: Luna-25 target (Boguslawsky)
sites.blurb: Russia's planned 2023 landing site. The spacecraft crashed before reaching it.

sites.name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
sites.blurb: Equatorial landing site: the Sun climbs high, and Earth sits almost still in the sky.

sites.name: Apollo 15 (Hadley–Apennine)
sites.blurb: Mid-latitude site at the foot of the Apennine mountains.

sites.name: SLIM (Shioli crater)
sites.blurb: JAXA's 2024 precision lander. It touched down upside-down, so its solar panels only worked when the Sun was in the west.

sites.name: Blue Ghost M1 (Mare Crisium)
sites.blurb: Firefly's 2025 lander. It operated a full lunar day and filmed sunset from the surface.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 (Von Kármán)
sites.blurb: The first far-side landing. Earth never rises here, so every bit of data goes through the Queqiao relay satellite.

sites.name: Chang'e 6 (Apollo basin)
sites.blurb: The first sample return from the far side (2024). It also had no direct-to-Earth link.
